Consult Summary:
- Acute gastroenteritis presenting with three days of watery diarrhea (5–6 times/day) preceded by vomiting and associated dehydration; managed with oral rehydration and symptomatic care with plans for follow-up if not improved.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Three days of diarrhoea with very watery stools, occurring 5–6 times daily; history of initial vomiting that has resolved; currently no significant abdominal pain.
- Onset, duration, progression: Symptoms began 3 days ago; vomiting occurred initially and resolved; now ongoing diarrhoea with dehydration symptoms and poor oral intake.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Frequent toilet visits with fluid intake not well tolerated; otherwise no specific triggers identified.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea at onset; felt feverish early on but currently not feverish; feels very weak; poor appetite; unable to drink much without causing further toilet visits.
- Review of systems: No blood in stool; no persistent fever reported; no headaches or muscle pains.
- Past Medical History: Asthma (blue inhaler, infrequently used).
- Medications: Inhaler (blue); no other regular medications documented; dose/route/frequency for medications not documented.
- Allergies: Not known.
- Social History: Lives alone; software engineer; off work for 3 days due to illness; drinks alcohol socially/infrequently; non-smoker.
- Family History: Father had hypertension; died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; mother has type 2 diabetes.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis
  - Plan:
    - Recommend oral fluid replacement and maintaining hydration (Dioralyte recommended).
    - Paracetamol for fever/weakness: dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Advise continued time off work for next day or two; return to work once diarrhoea-free for 24–48 hours.
    - If symptoms persist or do not improve, arrange follow-up in one week.
    - Monitor for dehydration and ability to tolerate fluids; seek care sooner if worsening or new symptoms (e.g., high fever, persistent vomiting, blood in stool) occur.
